"The mistake has been corrected," Elon Musk said, welcoming Huang back 11 days after his resignation.

Anthropic expects to pay SpaceX about $3.1 billion a month once it receives its full computing capacity, expected in December.

JPMorgan kept its $430 Tesla target, saying the rollout of FSD v15 underscored Tesla's lead in consumer autonomy.

Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) joined Monday's tech rally after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Elon Musk welcomed his return to Nvidia's helm, but investors may have a bigger reason to watch the relationship between the two tech billionaires, which is access to AI chips. An ARK Investment Management analyst said that Huang's influence over where scarce AI chips went mattered more than Nvidia's ability to finance its customers. Separately, TSLA shares also got a boost from the rollout of its latest full self driving software.

Tesla (TSLA) jumped 11.5% to $385.46, while SpaceX (SPCX) gained 4.4% to $133.35. Nvidia (NVDA) closed up 31.5%, adding nearly $1 trillion in market value after its board voted unanimously to bring Huang back 11 days after his resignation.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Musk Backs Huang When 'The Chips Are Down'

"It is done," Musk said on X. Minutes later, he shared Nvidia's announcement that Huang was returning as president, CEO and a board director. "The mistake has been corrected," Musk said.

Musk had backed Huang when a comeback was far from certain. Nvidia's board had rejected Huang's offer to return just six days before reversing course. As U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the reinstatement, Musk explained why he had stood by Huang. "Everyone is your friend when the chips are up, but those who support you when the chips are down are your real friends. Fair-weather friends are worthless," Musk said.

Later, sharing investor Gavin Baker's post about employees celebrating at Nvidia headquarters, he added, "Everyone I know at Nvidia wanted Jensen back and it shows."

However, governance questions pertain and Huang returns to Nvidia. The board's independent investigation is continuing, and Huang is scheduled to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec.3 as lawmakers scrutinize Nvidia's compliance with U.S. restrictions on chip exports to China.

ARK Says Huang Picked SpaceX For More Chips

Brett Winton, ARK Invest's chief futurist, said that investors were reading too much into a reported disagreement between Huang and Nvidia's CFO, Colette Kress. In his view, the decision facing Huang was whether to send more chips to SpaceX or finance smaller data-center builders still trying to secure power, schedule construction and win local support.

Tesla (NasdaqGS:TSLA) plans a wide release of its Full Self-Driving v15 software with the Tesla Reality View interface in the coming weeks.

Company insiders describe Tesla Reality View as a rebuilt driving visualisation system designed to give drivers a richer real time view of the car's surroundings.

People familiar with discussions say Tesla and SpaceX are exploring a potential merger that could value the combined group at about US$3.5 trillion.

The planned FSD v15 rollout and the potential US$3.5 trillion Tesla SpaceX merger might reshape the story, but they are only part of the picture. We have also flagged 3 warning signs for Tesla.

Tesla uses its electric vehicle platform as a testing ground for autonomous driving software, while its work on energy storage and global manufacturing gives any deeper tie up with SpaceX a broader hardware and infrastructure base than a pure software or internet player would have.

1 thing going right for Tesla that this headline doesn't cover.

Tesla's autonomy bet meets the SpaceX optionality story

The Tesla Narrative already hangs on turning heavy spending on FSD, robotaxis and AI hardware into profitable platforms. FSD v15 and the Tesla SpaceX merger talks both plug directly into that same bet; they just attack it from different angles.

"The main requirement for this thesis is that Tesla converts its heavy capital investment phase in robotaxis, Optimus, AI chips, and energy infrastructure into profitable, scaled platforms..."

See how the full story points towards a $418 fair value for Tesla.

The FSD v15 wide release with Tesla Reality View is the clearest proof point yet for the autonomy side of that story. It leans into the existing thesis that a larger base of paying FSD users can shift Tesla's mix toward higher margin software, something rivals like Mercedes and GM are also chasing with their own driver-assistance stacks.

The merger talks with SpaceX speak to the other half of the Narrative, which is optionality on AI infrastructure and energy. Combining Tesla's EV, storage and chip projects with SpaceX's launch assets and Starlink network fits the idea of a vertically integrated Physical AI platform, but analysts have already flagged that execution risk and regulatory scrutiny are key unresolved questions.

Putting this together, the news only really matters if you see it as confirming or weakening a single Narrative about Tesla turning today's costly autonomy and AI experiments into tomorrow's scaled businesses, which is what turns headlines into an investment call.

Josh Kohn-Lindquist, The Motley Fool

Up 4.74% to 7,238, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) exited correction territory in an historic rebound, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) surged 6.51% to 24,090 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) gained 3.01% to 49,595 as buyers returned ahead of the holiday week.

Today's biggest moves

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) skyrocketed 31.48% after the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO triggered a massive relief rally, while Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) soared 19.04% following newly secured multi-year customer agreements for memory supply and broader support from the AI trade rebound.

Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) climbed 11.60% on progress toward commercializing autonomous driving, whereas CrowdStrike (NASDAQ:CRWD) dropped 8.92% after the market digested news of the company's acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ:ZS) in an all-stock, $44 billion deal.

What this means for investors

After seven straight days of losses, the S&P 500 roared back on Monday, spurred by Jensen Huang being reinstated at Nvidia. Today's dramatic move helped the index exit correction territory, as it rose by its largest amount in over a year and a half.

Jensen's return spurs stock spikes: Most AI-related stocks tied to Nvidia soared today, with Nebius (NASDAQ:NBIS), CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), Dell (NYSE:DELL), Bloom Energy (NYSE:BE), and Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) all rising more than 15%.

CrowdStrike buys Zscaler: CrowdStrike dropped 9%, while Zscaler jumped 18% after the former announced it was acquiring the latter in an all-stock deal. Trading at a lofty valuation, I like CrowdStrike's decision to use its premium-priced equity to build out its cybersecurity platform. Now we need to watch for a successful integration if and when the deal closes in the second half of 2027, given the sheer size of the purchase.

Rocket Lab ends sell-off, skyrockets 9%: In a recent interview, Rocket Lab's CFO said they expect a "strong uplift in pricing within six to nine months" for its Electron launches, as SpaceX's (NASDAQ:SPCX) Falcon 9 is largely booked through late 2028 or early 2029. I think the market is rightfully optimistic about this outlook.

All in all, it was a great day for the markets and for investors, and it serves as a timely reminder of why Foolish investors focus on "time in the market rather than timing the market."

Shares of Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) stepped on the gas Monday morning, gaining as much as 13.9% in early trading. As of 2:18 p.m. ET, the stock was still up 12.3%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Two catalysts sent the electric vehicle (EV) specialist higher. The first was Wall Street conjecture about a potential merger with Space Exploration Technologies, aka SpaceX. The second was the rollout of the latest version of the company's self-driving software.

Image source: Tesla.

Part of something bigger

HSBC analyst Mike Tyndall upgraded Tesla stock to hold from reduce (sell) and more than doubled his price target to $359 from $157. However, the math suggests the analyst is playing catch-up, as that represented just 4% upside compared to the stock's closing price on Friday.

However, the analyst suggested that Tesla could fetch a hefty premium if it were to merge with SpaceX. Tyndall calculated a possible purchase price of $507 per share, representing a 33% premium over Tesla's 30-day average price. That represents potential upside of 47% compared to Friday's closing price. On the other hand, the analyst suggests that Tesla, as a stand-alone company, may be worth as little as $212, or 38% below Friday's close.

The commentary comes as the two companies hammer out the details of a potential blockbuster merger, which could come as soon as December, according to Bloomberg.

In other news, Tesla released the latest version of its Full Self-Driving (FSD) software, FSD V15, which CEO Elon Musk described as "a banger release." In a post on X this weekend, Musk said the upgrade provides "25x better handling of safety-critical cases."

The biggest unanswered question for Tesla investors is whether its robotaxi business will become a major profit center and cash cow for the company. Musk has predicted that robotaxi revenue will likely be "noticeable" by mid-2027, so that's an area investors will be watching carefully.

With Tesla's EV sales hitting the skids, an awful lot is riding on the company's robotaxi and robotics businesses. Until there's something concrete to report in either of those areas -- or until SpaceX announces plans to acquire Tesla -- the rest is just noise.

"No Synergies" in a SpaceX-Tesla Merger? Really? Starlink Just Showed Up in a Cybercab Roof ©@U.S. Air Force photo and SUMALI IBNU CHAMID from Alemedia.id via Canva
Key Takeaways

Jim Chanos says a SpaceX-Tesla merger has "no synergies" and would cut SpaceX's 2027 EPS by almost 40%.

Tesla has built a Starlink dish into the Cybercab's roof, so "no synergies" goes too far.

Tesla can buy Starlink service without a merger, just as SpaceX already buys Tesla's Megapack batteries without one.

Any deal comes down to its exchange ratio, and these ties don't justify a premium paid in SpaceX stock.

Jim Chanos doesn't think SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) and Tesla (TSLA:NASDAQ) have much to gain from each other.

Ron Baron told Andrew Ross Sorkin last week that Elon Musk will "do what's best for the companies, and for operating most efficiently." Chanos fired back on X that a merger "would cut SpaceX's growth rate by over 60%, and cut their 2027 estimated EPS by almost 40%."

Then another investor asked him why Musk, who has a big stake in each company, wouldn't want what's best for both. Chanos replied: "There are no synergies here. Musk runs both entities already."

No synergies? Take a look at the roof of a Cybercab.

Over the summer, Tesla's own Robotaxi account showed off the "First Cybercab with @Starlink integration." And the Cybercabs that started giving public rides in Dallas last week have a Starlink dish built right into the rear of the roof.

A robotaxi fleet is a Starlink customer

Tesla's AI chief Ashok Elluswamy also said over the summer that the Cybercab still drives itself on its own computer. The Starlink connection is there for navigation, customer service and fleet management. Musk then said Starlink would come to every Tesla model.

Think about what a car with no driver needs from a network. A rider wants help mid-trip. A support team needs to check on a car that stalled out past the last cell tower. Each of those runs over a connection that somebody gets paid for, and in a Tesla robotaxi fleet, that somebody would be Starlink.

SpaceX already knows how to sell to fleets, too. It has about 12,000 aircraft under contract for Starlink. Starlink's Connectivity segment earned $2.37 billion of SpaceX's $2.79 billion of third-quarter operating income. SpaceX buys from Tesla as well: it bought $480 million of Tesla Megapacks in the first nine months of 2026.

Tesla doesn't need a merger to buy Starlink

China’s Electric Cars Are Taking Over The World. Where Does That Leave Tesla?
A sleek smartphone displays the Tesla logo, while a laptop screen shows a portrait of Elon Musk.Elon Musk is the CEO and a co-founder of Tesla (Credit: Photo Courtesy: Creative Salim on Shutterstock.com)

Chinese automakers could export 12 million vehicles this year, according to analyst estimates, up from fewer than 1 million in 2020, as China's electric cars spread across the world.

For Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA), the boom brings an uncomfortable twist: its Shanghai factory now ships more cars abroad than it sells in China, while CEO Elon Musk bets the company's future on robotaxis.

China's EV Boom Goes Global

China is producing far more cars than it can sell at home, pushing its manufacturers to find buyers overseas.

Chinese car exports could reach 12 million this year, up from just 7.1 million in 2025, the Financial Times reported.

And Chinese manufacturers have a big advantage: they can build an electric car for around $20,000, compared with $31,000 in Europe, according to AlixPartners. Cheaper batteries, lower wages and lower energy costs help Chinese factories keep prices down, making it harder for Western manufacturers to compete.

Almost 70% of new cars sold in China are now electric or plug-in hybrids, more than double the share in Germany, France and the UK and more than 10 times the US level.

Tesla Is Following the Same Pattern

Tesla is facing the same pressure as its Chinese rivals. Sales in China are falling, making overseas markets increasingly important to its Shanghai factory.

Through October, Tesla exported about 421,000 vehicles from Shanghai, twice as many as a year earlier. That was more than the 390,000 it sold in China, where sales fell 15%, according to CnEVPost.

But escaping China's crowded car market isn't easy. Tesla's European registrations rose 50% through September, yet Chinese rival BYD registered even more vehicles there, including plug-in hybrids.

The same Chinese manufacturers squeezing Western brands in China are now competing with Tesla for customers abroad.

Musk's Answer: Robotaxis

Rather than win a price war with Chinese carmakers, Musk is betting Tesla's future on self-driving vehicles.

Earlier this month, Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production to make room for its Cybercab robotaxi. He later extended production through summer 2027 to clear existing orders.

But China is competing in autonomous driving too. XPeng plans to bring its assisted-driving technology to European cities next year, raising questions about how long Tesla can maintain a technological edge over its cheaper rivals.

What Traders Expect

On Kalshi, traders see an 80% chance Tesla exceeds 1.75 million deliveries in 2026, but just a 38% chance it tops 1.8 million.
